Mean Time to Recovery

Source: R/04_mttr.R
mttr.Rd

Computes the mean time to recovery of a discrete-time, finite-state Markov chain. Recovery is defined as the first time the chain leaves the set of non-operational states specified by down.

Usage

mttr(x, down)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

down

Nonempty integer-valued numeric vector of state positions, or character vector of state names, giving the non-operational states. Entries must be distinct and select a proper subset of the states. Input order is ignored; states are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric scalar giving the expected number of discrete-time transitions before the chain first enters a state outside down.

Details

These functions use mttf() and var_mttf() with down as the selected state set. The non-operational subchain must be transient, so that \(I_d-P_{\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}}\) is invertible. The asymptotic variance additionally requires an irreducible chain and treats the initial distribution as fixed.

The initial probabilities on down are not renormalized. Paths starting outside down have recovery time zero; to compute the mean conditional on starting down, supply an initial distribution supported on down.

Let \(\mathcal{D}\) denote the set of non-operational states, \(P_{\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}}\) be the submatrix of transition probabilities between non-operational states, \(d=|\mathcal{D}|\), and \(N=(I_d-P_{\mathcal{D},\mathcal{D}})^{-1}\). The mean time to recovery is computed as $$ \psi = a_{\mathcal{D}}^\mathsf{T} N \mathbf{1}_d, $$ where \(a_{\mathcal{D}}\) is the restriction of the initial distribution to the non-operational states and \(\mathbf{1}_d\) is a vector of ones.

Let \(\Sigma_{\mathcal{D}}\) be the submatrix of \(\Sigma_{\mathbf p}\) corresponding to transitions between non-operational states. Then: $$ \sqrt{n} \left\{ \widehat{\psi}_n-\psi \right\} \mathrel{\mathop{\longrightarrow}\limits^{d}} \mathcal{N} \left( 0, \sigma_\psi^2 \right), $$ where $$ \sigma_\psi^2 = D_\psi \Sigma_{\mathcal{D}} D_\psi^{\mathsf T}, $$ and $$ D_\psi = \left( a_{\mathcal{D}}^{\mathsf T}N \right) \mathbin{\otimes} \left( \mathbf{1}_d^{\mathsf T}N^{\mathsf T} \right). $$

The MTTR \(\psi\) is returned by this function. The asymptotic variance \(\sigma_\psi^2\) is returned by var_mttr().

References

Gavrilopoulos, G., Trevezas, S., and Votsi, I. (2026). Matrix asymptotic calculus for plug-in maximum likelihood estimators in finite Markov chains. arXiv preprint arXiv:2607.17161. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17161. See Proposition 11 for the MTTR differential and asymptotic variance.

Sadek, A., and Limnios, N. (2002). Asymptotic properties for maximum likelihood estimators for reliability and failure rates of Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 31(10), 1837–1861. doi:10.1081/STA-120014916 .

See also

mttf(), var_mttr()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
dimnames(P) <- list(c("working", "failed"), c("working", "failed"))
x <- MarkovChain(c(working = 0, failed = 1), P)
mttr(x, down = "failed")
#> [1] 3.333333
var_mttr(x, down = "failed")
#> [1] 64.81481
